Level one is CI as a deal aid.

Level two is CI as a forecast input.

Level three is where things get different. 

> Conversation data isn't something you go review. It's something your system acts on. The call ends and the next workflow triggers, the forecast updates, the coaching moment routes to the rep automatically.

That's where Salesloft Conversation Intelligence operates. And once you've seen it, reviewing transcripts and hoping someone does something with them is hard to go back to.

posts.content:
Most enterprise leaders are wrestling with the same question: Where's the ROI on our AI investment? It's a fair question. Budgets have gone in, expectations have been set, and for a lot of organizations the returns are harder to point to than the spend.

One of the more interesting things happening inside Clari + Salesloft right now is that the AI conversation has stopped being a technology conversation and started being an everyone conversation.

It's not just the revenue teams experimenting with what's possible. It's marketing, product, engineering, HR, finance; every function finding its own version of the problem AI can help solve. And every function learning something the others haven't figured out yet. 

What's become clear is that the value isn't just in what any one team discovers, but what happens when those discoveries start to travel.

A prompt that saves an engineer two hours of documentation work turns out to be useful for a CSM writing account summaries. A workflow a marketer built for campaign analysis turns out to have an application in sales coaching. 

The learning compounds in ways that nobody planned for, and faster than any top-down rollout could have engineered.

I think this is actually how AI value gets realized at scale: through the accumulation of small, practical discoveries that get shared across functions by people who are genuinely curious and willing to say "here's what I tried, here's what worked, and here's what didn't." That kind of organizational honesty is harder to build than the technology, and worth more when you have it.

We're still early, but the signal is encouraging. The investment starts paying back when the learning stops living in silos.

Most sales organisations don’t have a seller problem. What they have is a systems problem.

Over the last 20 years, we’ve layered process, reporting, tooling and admin onto revenue teams with the best of intentions. But somewhere along the way, many sellers stopped selling and started servicing the system around them.

You can see the consequences everywhere. High turnover. Huge amounts of seller time lost to administration. Forecasts that still lack confidence despite all the data available to us.

That’s where AI becomes genuinely interesting to me.
Not as another layer of tooling, but as a way to reduce friction, synthesise signals, and help sellers focus more of their time on customers.

Really enjoyed joining Cory Cotten-Potter on The B2B Revenue Executive Experience podcast to discuss where revenue organisations are getting stuck, why orchestration matters, and why better workflows matter just as much as better data.

"From the Pitch" Day 6 - Zach Powell, Senior Commercial Account Manager 🏆 

This series has highlighted our team's unique perspectives on coaching, visibility, execution, and integration.

Zach ties it together with the question every revenue leader should be asking right now: "Productivity for me doesn't mean just do more with less, but how do I get better with what I have?"

That's the right question. And it's harder to answer than it looks.

Getting better with what you have means your signals are sharper, your prioritization is smarter, and your reps are spending time on the things that actually move deals.

Zach's take on outbound was equally sharp: "Instead of hiring more reps to send more emails, let's send more specific emails about why you, why now."

When every outreach is informed by real buying signals — intent data, engagement patterns, deal history — reps don't need to send more. They need to send better.

This has been the week of From the Pitch — six finalists, six perspectives, one story: The future of revenue isn't more reporting. It's faster, smarter execution. That's the whole game.

Congratulations to all six finalists: Darian Amirpashaie, Dylan G.,  Jordan LeuVoy, Tommi Mann, Jennifer Englehardt, and Zach Powell. ⚽
